Count very hot days in each bushfire season

Source: R/count-hot-days.R
count_hot_days.Rd

For one city, counts the days in each fire season whose maximum temperature reached a chosen threshold, and records how complete the temperature record is for that season. Seasons with too many missing days are flagged rather than dropped, so users can see the gaps.

Usage

count_hot_days(
  temps,
  city,
  threshold = 35,
  months = c(9:12, 1:2),
  min_coverage = 0.9
)

Arguments

temps

A data frame of daily maximum temperatures with columns city, date and max_temp, such as fire_season_temps.

city

The name of one city in temps, for example "Melbourne".

threshold

A day counts as "hot" when its maximum temperature is at or above this value, in degrees Celsius. Defaults to 35.

months

The months of the season to include, as numbers. Defaults to the whole fire season, September to February (c(9:12, 1:2)). Use 9:11 for the spring build-up or c(12, 1, 2) for the summer peak.

min_coverage

The share of days in a season that must have a temperature reading for the season to be marked complete. Defaults to 0.9 (90%).

Value

A tibble with one row per fire season and columns:

city

City name.

season_start

Year the season starts (see fire_season()).

season

Season label, for example "2018-19".

days_possible

Calendar days in the selected months.

days_recorded

Days with a temperature reading.

coverage

days_recorded / days_possible.

hot_days

Days at or above threshold.

hottest

Highest maximum temperature in the season (degrees C).

complete

TRUE when coverage is at least min_coverage.

See also

count_exceedances() for any variable, threshold direction or season.

Examples

# Days of 35 degrees C or more in each Melbourne fire season
melb <- count_hot_days(fire_season_temps, "Melbourne")
tail(melb)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 9
#>   city      season_start season  days_possible days_recorded coverage hot_days
#>   <chr>            <int> <chr>           <int>         <int>    <dbl>    <int>
#> 1 Melbourne         2013 2013-14           181           181        1       12
#> 2 Melbourne         2014 2014-15           181           181        1        9
#> 3 Melbourne         2015 2015-16           182           182        1       11
#> 4 Melbourne         2016 2016-17           181           181        1       11
#> 5 Melbourne         2017 2017-18           181           181        1        8
#> 6 Melbourne         2018 2018-19           181           181        1       11
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: hottest <dbl>, complete <lgl>

# Only the most extreme days, in the summer peak
count_hot_days(fire_season_temps, "Adelaide", threshold = 40,
               months = c(12, 1, 2)) |>
  dplyr::slice_max(hot_days, n = 3)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 9
#>   city     season_start season  days_possible days_recorded coverage hot_days
#>   <chr>           <int> <chr>           <int>         <int>    <dbl>    <int>
#> 1 Adelaide         2013 2013-14            90            90        1       13
#> 2 Adelaide         2018 2018-19            90            90        1       10
#> 3 Adelaide         2008 2008-09            90            90        1        9
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: hottest <dbl>, complete <lgl>
